answer: To open a settlement seat, an agent must buy a numbered ivory chit, soak it in a one-time umber pigment lot, and book a passage through a metered river lock whose turbines stamp a live grain into the wet dye. The lock posts the grain against the pigment lot and chit serial. Reused chits, lots, or lock slots collapse to one operator and get slashed. Standing up N identities therefore costs N ivory blanks, N freshly mixed umber batches, and N real river transits with their wait and fuel bills.
